repos.name: elementalsouls / Claude-BugHunter
repos.description: A Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting and external red-team work - 82 skills, 15 slash commands, 681 disclosed-report patterns curated across 24 core vulnerability classes, plus enterprise identity + infrastructure attack matrices.

summary.goal: claude-bughunter is a skill bundle for Claude Code aimed at bug-bounty hunting and external red-team work, covering web application vulnerability detection, enterprise platform attack chains, and report triage/validation.
summary.usage: Install via the Claude Code plugin commands `/plugin marketplace add elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter` and `/plugin install claude-bughunter@elementalsouls`, or clone the repository with `git clone https://github.com/elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter.git` and run `bash scripts/install.sh` on macOS/Linux or `pwsh ./scripts/install.ps1` on Windows.
summary.pros: The bundle ships 83 skills and 15 slash commands drawing on 681 disclosed HackerOne report patterns (433 individually cited) across 24 vulnerability classes, plus enterprise identity/infrastructure attack matrices and Burp MCP integration.
summary.cons: By design the bundle explicitly excludes internal Active Directory attacks, C2 frameworks, post-exploitation/persistence techniques, and evasion tooling, so users needing those capabilities must look elsewhere; Anthropic's runtime safeguards can also block even authorized offensive-security work by default.
summary.fit: Given its stated focus on internet-facing external attack surfaces, the bundle appears best suited for bug bounty hunters and external red-team operators rather than teams needing internal network or AD-focused tooling.

repos.name: obra / superpowers
repos.description: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.

summary.goal: Superpowers is presented as a complete software development methodology for coding agents, built on composable skills plus initial instructions that make sure the agent uses them.
summary.usage: Installation reportedly differs by coding-agent harness, and the README indicates separate installation is needed for each one in use. For Claude Code, the documented command is /plugin install superpowers@claude-plugins-official via the official marketplace.
summary.pros: Skills appear to trigger automatically once installed, without extra invocation steps, and the workflow seems to enforce mandatory practices such as RED-GREEN-REFACTOR test-driven development and code review between tasks rather than treating them as optional suggestions.
summary.cons: A harness-specific install step suggests users running agents in multiple tools must repeat setup separately for each; the Hermes Agent section also notes it lacks a post-compaction hook, so a very long first session could reportedly lose the startup bootstrap.
summary.fit: This project seems best suited to users running coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini CLI, or similar supported harnesses who want an enforced, multi-stage development workflow rather than ad-hoc coding assistance.

repos.name: HKUDS / CLI-Anything
repos.description: "CLI-Anything: Making ALL Software Agent-Native" -- CLI-Hub: https://clianything.cc/

summary.goal: CLI-Anything is an open-source project (Apache 2.0) that converts software with an available codebase into agent-native command-line interfaces, so AI agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, OpenClaw, and Pi can operate real applications through structured CLI commands instead of GUI automation.
summary.usage: Users can browse and install community-built CLIs with `pip install cli-anything-hub` followed by `cli-hub install <name>`, or generate a new CLI harness by adding the Claude Code marketplace (`/plugin marketplace add HKUDS/CLI-Anything`, `/plugin install cli-anything`) and running `/cli-anything ./gimp` to drive the 7-phase generator; Python 3.10+ is required.
summary.pros: The README reports 2,461 passing tests across the generated harnesses, Apache 2.0 licensing, and built-in JSON output for machine consumption alongside a human-readable REPL mode, with support spanning multiple agent platforms including Claude Code, OpenCode, Cursor, Codex, Hermes, and Reasonix.
summary.cons: The documented Limitations section states that CLI-Anything relies on frontier-class models (e.g., Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4) for reliable generation, requires access to the target software's source code rather than compiled binaries, and often needs iterative `/refine` runs to reach production-quality coverage.
summary.fit: Based on the documented scope, the project appears best suited for teams or developers who want to expose existing open-source or internal software to AI agents without building custom APIs, though actual results may depend on the capability of the underlying agent model and the availability of source code.

repos.name: jingyaogong / minimind
repos.description: 🧠 两小时从 0 训出你的 64M 大模型。Train your own 64M LLM from scratch in 2 hours.

summary.goal: MiniMind's goal is to let individuals train a very small (~64M parameter) language model entirely from scratch, at an estimated cost of about 3 RMB and around 2 hours on a single NVIDIA 3090 GPU, covering pretraining, SFT, LoRA, RLHF/DPO, and RLAIF (PPO/GRPO/CISPO), Tool Use, and Agentic RL, implemented natively in PyTorch.
summary.usage: Clone the repository and install dependencies with `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/jingyaogong/minimind` and `pip install -r requirements.txt`; run inference via `python eval_llm.py --load_from ./minimind-3`, and run training stages such as `cd trainer && python train_pretrain.py` or `python train_full_sft.py`.
summary.pros: Core training algorithms (pretraining, SFT, LoRA, DPO, distillation) are implemented natively in PyTorch without relying on high-level third-party wrappers, while the project documents compatibility with transformers, trl, peft, and inference engines like llama.cpp, vllm, and ollama, plus multi-GPU DDP/DeepSpeed training with wandb/SwanLab logging.
summary.cons: The README's own benchmark results show weak English-language performance because training data is weighted toward Chinese, and the custom tokenizer's vocabulary is limited to 6,400 tokens, notably smaller than tokenizers used by comparable open models.
summary.fit: This appears best suited to learners and researchers wanting a hands-on, reproducible path through full LLM training pipelines on a single consumer GPU, rather than to those seeking a production-ready model with strong multilingual or large-scale capability.

repos.name: cursor / plugins
repos.description: Cursor plugin specification and official plugins

summary.goal: The cursor/plugins repository is an official collection of Cursor plugins for developer tools, frameworks, and SaaS products. Each plugin exists as a standalone directory at the repository root with its own .cursor-plugin/plugin.json manifest.
summary.usage: The repo is organized as a multi-plugin marketplace: the root .cursor-plugin/marketplace.json file lists all plugins, and each plugin folder contains its own .cursor-plugin/plugin.json manifest plus optional skills/, rules/, and mcp.json files. The README documents this layout but does not appear to list explicit installation or run commands, so actual usage likely depends on how Cursor loads these manifest files.
summary.pros: The marketplace spans well over one hundred plugins across categories such as Developer Tools, Productivity, Integrations, and Finance and Legal, covering tools like GitHub, Google Workspace apps, Salesforce, and Playwright, giving broad coverage of common developer and business workflows.
summary.cons: Individual plugin entries carry their own operational limits; for instance, the QuickBooks plugin's payment-link sending is documented as limited to the US and Canada, which may constrain usefulness for teams operating in other regions, and similar region- or account-specific constraints likely apply to other third-party integrations without being summarized at the top level.
summary.fit: This repository appears suited to teams and developers building or extending Cursor plugins who want a reference catalog of manifest and folder conventions, rather than users seeking a single standalone application or service.

repos.name: firecrawl / firecrawl
repos.description: Knowledge infrastructure to make your agents smarter. Search, scrape and access 550+ data providers through one API.

summary.goal: Firecrawl is knowledge infrastructure intended to make AI agents smarter by turning websites into clean markdown and structured data. The README describes three ways to use it: Firecrawl Local (a self-hosted binary), Firecrawl Cloud (a hosted service), and full self-hosting of the server from this repository.
summary.usage: Firecrawl Local installs via `cargo install firecrawl-local` (requires Rust and a C compiler), and commands like `firecrawl-local scrape`, `firecrawl-local crawl`, and `firecrawl-local serve` handle scraping, crawling, and running a local API on port 3002. The Python and Node SDKs install with `pip install firecrawl` and `npm install firecrawl`.
summary.pros: The README states Firecrawl Cloud covers 96% of the web including JS-heavy pages, with a P95 latency of 3.4 seconds, and returns LLM-ready markdown, structured JSON, and screenshots. Firecrawl Keyless offers 1,000 free credits a month without an API key or signup.
summary.cons: Running Firecrawl Local requires installing Rust and a C compiler toolchain (e.g., Xcode command line tools or build-essential), an extra setup step compared to using the hosted Cloud service. The core server is also licensed under AGPL-3.0, a copyleft license that may impose obligations in some deployment scenarios, though SDKs are MIT licensed.
summary.fit: This project appears suited for teams building AI agents that need web data, offering options from a single local binary to a fully self-hosted server with Docker Compose, Redis, PostgreSQL, and a browser service. Self-hosting likely requires more operational effort than using Firecrawl Cloud directly.

repos.name: nginx / nginx
repos.description: The official NGINX Open Source repository.

summary.goal: NGINX is described as a widely used web server that also functions as a high performance load balancer, reverse proxy, API gateway, and content cache. It is free and open source software distributed under a simplified 2-clause BSD-like license.
summary.usage: The README documents cloning the source with `git clone https://github.com/nginx/nginx.git`, then running `auto/configure` followed by `make` to build, and `sudo make install` to install the binary (installed into `/usr/local/nginx/`). The compiled binary can be run with `sudo /usr/local/nginx/sbin/nginx`, and operation can be verified with `curl localhost`.
summary.pros: Binary packages are available for all major operating systems and Linux distributions, and official package repositories ensure the most recent release, features, fixes, and security patches. Dynamic modules, such as NGINX JavaScript (njs), can be installed after the core binaries are built without recompiling, and worker processes can auto-scale to available CPU cores.
summary.cons: Building from source requires installing dependency libraries such as `libpcre3-dev` and `zlib1g-dev` beforehand (with additional libraries like `libssl-dev` needed for SSL support), which suggests the build process has prerequisites that must be satisfied before compilation succeeds. The README also notes that the Windows implementation is at the Proof-of-Concept stage and is intended only for development and testing, not production use.
summary.fit: This project appears suited for users needing a web server, reverse proxy, load balancer, or API gateway on Linux, FreeBSD, or similar Unix-like systems, with precompiled packages simplifying deployment. Given the Proof-of-Concept status noted for Windows, it may be less suited for production Windows deployments.

repos.name: openvinotoolkit / openvino
repos.description: OpenVINO™ is an open source toolkit for optimizing and deploying AI inference

summary.goal: OpenVINO (openvinotoolkit/openvino) is documented as an open-source software toolkit for optimizing and deploying deep learning models, aimed at inference optimization for computer vision, automatic speech recognition, generative AI, and natural language processing tasks.
summary.usage: The README documents installing via `pip install -U openvino`, and verifying the install by running `import openvino as ov; print(ov.__version__)` in Python.
summary.pros: Documented strengths include broad platform compatibility (CPU x86/ARM, GPU, and Intel NPU accelerators), support for models from PyTorch, TensorFlow, ONNX, Keras, PaddlePaddle, and JAX/Flax, and an ecosystem of integrations such as NNCF, Optimum Intel, LangChain, and LlamaIndex.
summary.cons: The README states that OpenVINO collects software performance and usage data by default (directly or via Google Analytics 4), so users must explicitly run `opt_in_out --opt_out` if they want to disable this telemetry.
summary.fit: Given its documented device and framework support, OpenVINO appears best suited for teams deploying inference workloads across CPU, GPU, and NPU hardware for vision, speech, or generative AI tasks, though the README recommends checking system requirements and supported devices before setup.

repos.name: cathrynlavery / diagram-design
repos.description: Editorial diagram design for Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Factory Droid, Qoder, and Pi. 52 diagram types. Self-contained HTML + SVG. No shadows. No Mermaid slop.

summary.goal: Diagram Design is an agent skill that generates diagrams as a single self-contained HTML file with inline SVG, matched to a user's brand. It covers 52 diagram types, each in three variants (minimal light, minimal dark, full-editorial), and can also redraw existing diagrams from draw.io, Mermaid, Excalidraw, or PlantUML sources.
summary.usage: Install with `npx skills add cathrynlavery/diagram-design`, or in Claude Code run `/plugin marketplace add cathrynlavery/diagram-design` followed by `/plugin install diagram-design@diagram-design`. After installation, users ask their agent in plain language (e.g., for an architecture diagram or sequence diagram), and the agent writes one `.html` file that opens by double-clicking.
summary.pros: Output is a single file with no build step, JavaScript, or external image dependency, and loads fonts from Google Fonts as its only network request (or none, with system fonts). It supports brand onboarding by extracting a site's palette and fonts, and works across many Agent Skills hosts, including Cursor, Claude Code, Codex, and GitHub Copilot.
summary.cons: Output quality depends on the model running it, and the same prompt can lay out a diagram differently between runs. The result is not an editable source format: there is no text to diff in a pull request and no canvas to drag shapes on. PNG export additionally requires a one-time setup step (`pip install playwright && playwright install chromium`).
summary.fit: The README positions it for diagrams meant to be published, such as blog posts or decks, rather than documentation that lives in Git and changes frequently, for which it states Mermaid remains the better fit.

repos.name: mvanhorn / last30days-skill
repos.description: AI agent skill that researches any topic across Reddit, X, YouTube, HN, Polymarket, and the web - then synthesizes a grounded summary

summary.goal: last30days is an AI agent-led research skill that searches Reddit, X, YouTube, TikTok, Polymarket, GitHub, and other platforms in parallel, then synthesizes the results into a single brief ranked by real engagement such as upvotes and real money rather than editorial curation.
summary.usage: In Claude Code, install with `/plugin marketplace add mvanhorn/last30days-skill` followed by `/plugin install last30days`; other supported hosts such as Codex, Cursor, Copilot, and Gemini CLI can install via `npx skills add mvanhorn/last30days-skill -g`. Running `/last30days <topic>` once also triggers a setup wizard that can unlock additional sources.
summary.pros: Reddit, Hacker News, Polymarket, and GitHub work immediately with no configuration, and patent filings or careers pages are included automatically for company topics. Results are scored by actual audience engagement and real-money signals rather than SEO or editorial ranking.
summary.cons: Several listed sources (X, TikTok, Xiaohongshu, Telegram, Trustpilot, Amazon) depend on opt-in credentials, installed CLIs, or browser sessions, so the set of sources actually searched likely varies by topic and configured keys. Claude Desktop installation also requires Python 3.12+ on the host.
summary.fit: The project appears aimed at people who want a fast read on recent community activity before meetings, sales calls, or trips, and it is documented to install across Claude Code, Claude Desktop, claude.ai, Grok, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, and OpenClaw.

repos.name: google-labs-code / stitch-skills
repos.description: A library of Agent Skills designed to work with the Stitch MCP server. Each skill follows the Agent Skills open standard, for compatibility with coding agents such as Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Cursor.

summary.goal: stitch-skills is a repository of agent skills and plugins for Google Stitch, following the Agent Skills open standard. It is documented as compatible with coding agents including Codex, Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Cursor, and OpenCode (manual install).
summary.usage: For Codex, run `codex plugin marketplace add google-labs-code/stitch-skills --ref main` (optionally with --sparse paths) to add the marketplace. For Claude Code, run `npx plugins add google-labs-code/stitch-skills --scope project --target claude-code`. To install individual skills, run `npx skills add google-labs-code/stitch-skills`.
summary.pros: The repository separates functionality into three plugins (stitch-design, stitch-build, stitch-utilities), letting users install only the skills they need, and supports sparse checkouts to speed up installation.
summary.cons: Skills require a separately configured Stitch MCP server with its own credentials and environment variables before they can run, and selectively installed skills may need manually resolved inter-dependencies.
summary.fit: This appears best suited for teams already using Google Stitch alongside a supported coding agent; OpenCode users should note it needs manual skill and MCP setup rather than the marketplace flow used by Codex or Claude Code.

repos.name: mjmirza / app-store-compliance
repos.description: Avoid common App Store and Google Play rejections. Open playbook and pre-submission guard with 124 documented rejection patterns and fixes, privacy manifest and Data safety checks, 112 tracked deadlines (EU AI Act, DSA, COPPA, age laws), and a skill for AI coding agents.

summary.goal: This repository documents a pre-submission compliance playbook and guard script meant to catch App Store and Google Play rejection causes before a human reviewer does, covering both iOS and Android apps. It is explicitly described as a reference and scan, not a guarantee of approval.
summary.usage: Usage begins by cloning the repository with `git clone https://github.com/mjmirza/app-store-compliance ~/repositories/app-store-compliance`, then scanning a project with `bash ~/repositories/app-store-compliance/agent-os/hooks/app-store-compliance-guard.sh "/path/to/your/app"`. A separate installer can also wire the same guard into AI coding tools such as Claude Code so it runs automatically before submit commands.
summary.pros: Documented strengths include flagging rejection risk before Apple or Google review, mapping each rejection pattern to a specific guideline and fix, prioritizing the two most common rejection causes (a working demo account and an accurate privacy declaration), and supporting both developers and non-developers through a plain-language checklist.
summary.cons: One documented trade-off is that the rule data is time-sensitive: the guard reports a `Rule pack STALE.` state once its rules exceed 60 days old, requiring a `git pull` before rescanning. Also, a `CLEAR.` verdict is not an approval, since the automated scan cannot verify account- or listing-level details.
summary.fit: Based on the described hook and installer options, this appears best suited for developers and teams already using AI coding assistants such as Claude Code who want an automated pre-submission guard, as well as non-developers willing to follow a manual checklist; it does not seem intended to replace manual review of account and store-listing readiness.

repos.name: Tracer-Cloud / opensre
repos.description: The open-source agent for CI/CD reliability.

summary.goal: OpenSRE is an open-source CLI agent built to investigate CI/CD pipeline failures: it reads a failed run's logs, traces the root cause, and pushes a fix for review. It is described as self-hosted and designed to work with your own LLM models.
summary.usage: Install it on macOS or Linux with `curl -fsSL https://install.opensre.com | bash -s -- -gh`, or the PowerShell equivalent on Windows, then launch the interactive shell with `opensre`. For one-off, non-interactive runs (e.g. in a CI script), use `opensre ask "why is checkout-api slow?"`.
summary.pros: The agent separates CI-caused failures from code-caused ones and gives evidence-linked answers rather than just a failure notice. It also connects to 60+ integrations spanning LLM providers, observability platforms (Grafana, Datadog, CloudWatch), infrastructure (Kubernetes, AWS), and incident tools (Slack, PagerDuty, GitHub).
summary.cons: The project carries a public-alpha status, so core workflows are described as usable but not yet fully stable, and APIs/integrations may still change. Self-hosted deployment also appears to require configuring your own LLM_PROVIDER and API key rather than a turnkey managed service.
summary.fit: Given its self-hosted, bring-your-own-model design and CI/CD/incident-response focus, OpenSRE seems best suited to engineering teams already running CI pipelines and observability stacks who want an agent they control, rather than teams seeking a fully managed, zero-setup SaaS tool.

repos.name: toeverything / AFFiNE
repos.description: There can be more than Notion and Miro. AFFiNE(pronounced [ə‘fain]) is a next-gen knowledge base that brings planning, sorting and creating all together. Privacy first, open-source, customizable and ready to use.

summary.goal: AFFiNE is described as an open-source, local-first, privacy-focused all-in-one workspace positioned as an alternative to Notion and Miro, merging documents, canvas/whiteboard, and databases into one platform.
summary.usage: The README documents self-hosting via Docker, with one-click "Deploy to Render" and "Run on Sealos" options, plus documentation at https://docs.affine.pro/self-host-affine; building from source is covered in BUILDING.md, and GitHub Codespaces is also supported.
summary.pros: Documented strengths include local-first data ownership, real-time collaborative sync across web and cross-platform clients, and a free, self-hostable MIT-licensed Community Edition (CE).
summary.cons: The Enterprise Edition (EE), which would add advanced admin, audit, and SSO features, is stated as not yet published, so those capabilities are currently unavailable; contributors must also sign a Contributor License Agreement (CLA) before any pull request can be merged.
summary.fit: This suggests AFFiNE fits individuals or teams wanting a self-hosted, privacy-oriented Notion/Miro alternative, though organizations needing enterprise SSO or advanced admin/audit tooling would need to wait, since EE is not yet released.

repos.name: XiaoYouChR / Ghost-Downloader-3
repos.description: The only downloader you need. 下载器的集大成者。

summary.goal: Ghost Downloader 3 is a download manager that handles multiple protocols, including HTTP, Magnet/BT, FTP, M3U8, MPEG-DASH, eD2k, YouTube, and Bilibili (with clip selection, quality options, and subtitles), as well as GitHub and HuggingFace downloads with mirror acceleration. It runs natively on Windows, macOS, Linux, and Android.
summary.usage: A command-line tool is installed from inside the app via Settings -> Command Line Tool. Example commands include `ghd probe <url>` to preview a URL without starting a download, and `ghd add <url>...` to add and start download tasks.
summary.pros: It consolidates many download protocols and sources into a single application, provides an `aria2`-compatible RPC API so third-party tools can control tasks, and pairs with a browser extension that lets detected downloads continue seamlessly in the desktop app.
summary.cons: Each platform carries a minimum version requirement: Windows `10+`, macOS `13.0+`, Linux `glibc 2.35+`, and Android `9.0+`. The README also notes that Qt `6.6+` no longer supports CPUs without the AVX instruction set, which could exclude some older systems from running the app.
summary.fit: The project is distributed under the `GPL v3.0` License, which suggests it is intended for users open to working within open-source licensing terms, though the README does not detail enterprise or commercial-use considerations.

repos.name: zhouxiaoka / autoclip
repos.description: AutoClip｜一个链接，一键出片。开源 AI 视频剪辑桌面工具，将播客、访谈、课程等长视频自动剪成短视频，生成字幕、封面和发布文案，适配抖音、小红书、TikTok、Reels 与 YouTube Shorts。Open-source AI video clipping & content repurposing.

summary.goal: AutoClip is an open-source tool that converts a single video link into finished output—video, cover image, and publishing caption—rendered locally on the user's computer. It supports Douyin, Xiaohongshu, TikTok, Reels, YouTube Shorts, Bilibili, and YouTube. The software is free; cloud models are billed by usage.
summary.usage: AutoClip can run as a desktop app (macOS Apple Silicon or Windows x64), via Docker Compose, or through a CLI/MCP interface requiring Python 3.10+ and FFmpeg. Deployment commands include `docker compose up -d --build` for the Docker/Web setup and `autoclip --version` to verify the CLI installation.
summary.pros: It auto-generates up to 10 qualified clips per platform, each paired with a cover image, title, description, hashtags, and a ZIP publishing kit, while matching aspect ratio and duration to the chosen platform. Editing and rendering stay on the local machine, and users can choose their own analysis model and subtitle source, including author subtitles, local Whisper/SenseVoice, or cloud transcription.
summary.cons: Desktop installers are not yet code-signed or notarized, so new releases may trigger Windows SmartScreen warnings or antivirus false positives, and there is currently no desktop installer for Intel Macs, which instead require Docker or CLI usage.
summary.fit: The tool appears best suited to individual creators or small teams producing short clips from interviews, podcasts, or talks on their own hardware or via self-hosted Docker/CLI/Agent integration. As a solo-maintained project without guaranteed response times, it may be less suited to users requiring dedicated support.

repos.name: backnotprop / plannotator
repos.description: The workspace to stay in the loop and on top of agents - shape, decide, plan, annotate, review code, share with team, and send all feedback to agents with one click.

summary.goal: Plannotator is a local, browser-based review surface that lets developers annotate and respond to output from AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Kiro, Droid, Amp, DeepSeek Harness, and Pi. It surfaces plans, specs, HTML artifacts, and diffs so feedback can be sent back to the agent.
summary.usage: Install with `curl -fsSL https://plannotator.ai/install.sh | bash` on macOS/Linux/WSL, or `irm https://plannotator.ai/install.ps1 | iex` in Windows PowerShell. After installation, slash commands such as `/plannotator-review` (review uncommitted changes or a PR/MR URL) and `/plannotator-annotate` (annotate a file, folder, or URL) open the review UI in the browser.
summary.pros: It integrates with a wide range of coding agents and version control systems, including Git, GitButler, Jujutsu, Perforce, GitHub, and GitLab, and supports guided reviews that split large diffs into chapters. Released binaries ship with SHA256 checksums and, from version v0.17.2, SLSA provenance attestations.
summary.cons: In remote mode the local server listens on every network interface (0.0.0.0) without requiring login, so the documentation cautions that anyone able to reach the port could use it even through an SSH tunnel. Some integrations also appear to carry agent-specific prerequisites, such as Gemini CLI 0.36.0+.
summary.fit: Because review state is tied to a local server and browser session, the tool appears best suited to individual developers already using one of the supported coding agents locally. A team-oriented sharing feature ('Workspaces') is still listed as waitlist-only, suggesting multi-user collaboration is not yet broadly available.

repos.name: GoogleChrome / modern-web-guidance-src
repos.description: Keep your coding agent up to date with the latest web best practices

summary.goal: Modern Web Guidance is a set of skills that embeds web platform expertise, best practices, and browser compatibility data directly into coding agents' context windows. It aims to steer agents away from legacy JavaScript patterns toward native, modern web platform APIs focused on performance, accessibility, and responsible fallbacks.
summary.usage: Install via `npx modern-web-guidance@latest install`, which runs an interactive wizard and requires Node.js 22 or later. Without installing, commands like `npx modern-web-guidance@latest search "<query>"` and `npx modern-web-guidance@latest legacy-scan .` let users search guides or scan a codebase for legacy patterns.
summary.pros: Guides are described as token-efficient, with evals used to prune content models already know. Local semantic search runs offline via a zero-dependency embedding model, requiring no API keys. Published eval snapshots (e.g., Nov 8) show agent performance improving from unguided to guided use, with some agent/model combinations rising from 57% to 88%.
summary.cons: Telemetry collection appears enabled by default, sending anonymous usage data (installation counts, guide IDs, search queries) unless a user sets `DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1`; this may matter in privacy-sensitive setups. Separately, the README notes Claude Code plugin installs via the `claude-plugins-official` marketplace were stranded at v0.0.194, requiring a manual marketplace switch to receive updates.
summary.fit: Based on the described integrations (Claude Code, Codex, Grok Build CLI, Antigravity, Copilot CLI, Kimi Code, Pi), the project seems aimed at developers using AI coding agents across multiple platforms who want guidance embedded in-agent rather than a standalone tool, though suitability likely depends on which agent CLI is already in use.

repos.name: alibaba / open-code-review
repos.description: Secure, fast, efficient, battle-tested at Alibaba's scale. Hybrid architecture code review tool: deterministic pipelines + LLM Agent, precise line-level comments, built-in multi-language ruleset (NPE, thread-safety, XSS, SQL injection), OpenAI & Anthropic compatible.

summary.goal: alibaba/open-code-review (Open Code Review) is an AI-powered code review CLI tool originally built as Alibaba Group's internal assistant, now open-sourced. It reads Git diffs and sends changed files to a configurable LLM through an agent to produce structured, line-level review comments.
summary.usage: Install the agent skills with `npx skills add alibaba/open-code-review`, or install the CLI globally with `npm install -g @alibaba-group/open-code-review` (requires Git >= 2.41). Run `ocr review` to review Git diffs, or `ocr scan` to review whole files; native mode needs a configured OCR model provider, while delegation mode uses the host agent's own model.
summary.pros: According to the README's benchmark, cross-validated by 80+ senior engineers across 50 repositories, 200 pull requests, 10 languages, and 1,505 annotated ground-truth issues, Open Code Review reports higher Precision and F1 than Claude Code with the same model while using only about 1/9 of the tokens.
summary.cons: The same benchmark states Recall is lower than general-purpose agents, described as a deliberate trade-off favoring precision over noise; native review mode also requires configuring a separate OCR model provider beyond the base CLI installation.
summary.fit: Open Code Review may suit teams already using Git-based workflows and agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or Kimi Code who want automated review comments; it likely presumes an existing Git repository and, for native mode, an LLM provider credential.

repos.name: ChromeDevTools / chrome-devtools-mcp
repos.description: Chrome DevTools for coding agents

summary.goal: chrome-devtools-mcp is a Model-Context-Protocol (MCP) server and CLI that lets coding agents (such as Antigravity, Claude, Cursor, or Copilot) control and inspect a live Chrome browser for automation, debugging, and performance analysis.
summary.usage: Add an MCP client config that runs `npx -y chrome-devtools-mcp@latest`, or install the package globally with `npm i chrome-devtools-mcp@latest -g` to use the `chrome-devtools` CLI (e.g. `chrome-devtools navigate_page`).
summary.pros: It provides performance trace recording via Chrome DevTools, network/console inspection with source-mapped stack traces, and reliable automation through Puppeteer that waits for action results.
summary.cons: The README states only Google Chrome and Chrome for Testing are officially supported, so other Chromium-based browsers may behave unpredictably; usage statistics are also collected by default unless explicitly disabled.
summary.fit: This tool appears suited for developers integrating browser debugging and automation into AI coding agents, and requires Node.js LTS, a current stable Chrome, and npm.

repos.name: tradermonty / claude-trading-skills
repos.description: Claude Code skills for equity investors and traders — market analysis, technical charting, economic calendars, screeners, and trading strategy development.

summary.goal: Claude Trading Skills is a Claude Skills-based trading workflow toolkit for time-constrained individual investors. Its stated goal is not to outsource buy/sell decisions to AI, but to structure market review, risk management, trade planning, journaling, and continuous improvement.
summary.usage: Users can download the `.skill` package from the latest GitHub Release, or clone the repository and copy a skill folder into `~/.claude/skills/` for Claude Code. Packages for distribution are rebuilt with `python3 scripts/package_skills.py --skill <skill-name>`.
summary.pros: It ships a "No API Key Starter Path" of five skills (market-breadth-analyzer, uptrend-analyzer, position-sizer, trader-memory-core, signal-postmortem) that run on public CSVs and local files, letting users review markets, size trades, journal, and review outcomes without a paid market-data API subscription.
summary.cons: Several workflows and screeners depend on optional paid integrations such as FMP, FINVIZ Elite ($39.50/month or $299.50/year), or Alpaca; going beyond the basic no-API path for screeners or portfolio workflows may require one of these subscriptions.
summary.fit: The toolkit appears best suited for long-term, ETF, and dividend-focused investors who add disciplined swing trading as a satellite strategy, rather than for fully automated trading, signal outsourcing, or short-term scalping.

repos.name: ag-ui-protocol / ag-ui
repos.description: AG-UI: the Agent-User Interaction Protocol. Bring Agents into Frontend Applications.

summary.goal: AG-UI is described as an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how AI agents connect to user-facing applications, replacing custom per-framework wiring with one bi-directional event stream so agents can power web, mobile, terminal, or Slack clients.
summary.usage: A new app can be scaffolded with `npx create-ag-ui-app@latest`, or developers can speak the protocol directly by installing `pip install ag-ui-protocol fastapi uvicorn` for a Python agent server and `npm install @ag-ui/client tsx` for a TypeScript client, per the documented quick-start example.
summary.pros: The README states AG-UI 1.0 has a stable, frozen specification backed by a JSON Schema with TypeScript, Python, and .NET SDKs generated from it, is backwards compatible between 0.x and 1.0, and is adopted by Google, Microsoft, Amazon, and Oracle with integrations across many agent frameworks.
summary.cons: The Python agent quick-start requires Python 3.9+ and the TypeScript client requires Node.js 20+, and the generated CopilotKit templates call OpenAI, requiring an `OPENAI_API_KEY` to be set before running.
summary.fit: AG-UI is positioned as complementary to MCP (tools/context) and A2A (agent-to-agent), serving specifically the agent-to-user connection layer, suggesting it fits projects needing a framework-agnostic transport for streaming chat, shared state, or human-in-the-loop UI rather than tool-calling or inter-agent communication alone.

repos.name: meta / astryx
repos.description: An open source design system that's fully customizable and agent ready

summary.goal: Astryx is an open source design system built on React 19+ and StyleX, developed internally at Meta over eight years and reportedly powering 13,000+ apps. It provides 150+ accessible components, theming, dark mode, templates, and a CLI, aimed at both human developers and AI coding assistants building interfaces consistently.
summary.usage: Install with `npm install @astryxdesign/core @astryxdesign/theme-neutral @stylexjs/stylex` (adding `@astryxdesign/cli` as a dev dependency), then run `npx @astryxdesign/cli init` once to set up styles, a theme, and project guide files like AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md.
summary.pros: Components can be composed or 'swizzled' to eject full source for deeper customization, and styling overrides work via plain `className` with Tailwind, CSS modules, or plain CSS, avoiding lock-in to StyleX despite it being used internally.
summary.cons: The project is explicitly labeled 'Currently in Beta,' which suggests the API and components may still change before a stable release. Related packages—@astryxdesign/lab, @astryxdesign/vega, and @astryxdesign/charts—are either unpublished or available only under the @canary npm tag, indicating no stable release yet for those.
summary.fit: Astryx requires React 19 or later as a peer dependency, so it likely fits best for projects already running a recent React version rather than legacy codebases; its design and CLI appear intended to be used identically by human developers and AI coding assistants.

repos.name: pookjw / HermesEnabler
repos.description: Enable Hermès Watch Faces on any Apple Watch devices

summary.goal: HermesEnabler2 appears to be a tool for installing a developer-mode-related enabler app onto a paired Apple Watch; the README states it is supported on watchOS 27.0 through 27.3 beta 1.
summary.usage: On macOS, download the IPA from GitHub Releases and sideload it with Sideloadly, or build and run HermesEnabler2.xcodeproj directly in Xcode; after installing, open HermesEnabler2 on the Watch and follow its in-app steps. On Windows, download watchbridge-windows.zip from WatchBridge Releases, extract it, and run WatchBridge.exe to prepare Developer Mode and install the same IPA.
summary.pros: Two independent installation paths are documented — sideloading or Xcode on macOS, and the separate WatchBridge tool on Windows — and once the iPhone and Watch are paired over USB, subsequent installs and renewals can proceed over Wi-Fi.
summary.cons: The README states watchOS 26 is not supported, limiting compatibility to watchOS 27.0 through 27.3 beta 1; it also notes WatchBridge is an unsigned, community-maintained tool unaffiliated with Apple or this project, and that it supports only one paired Watch at a time.
summary.fit: This seems intended for users with an Apple Watch on one of the specific supported watchOS versions who are willing to sideload unsigned software; the README explicitly states use is at the user's own risk.

repos.name: we-promise / sure
repos.description: The personal finance app for everyone (by everyone)

summary.goal: Sure is a personal finance application and community-maintained fork of the discontinued Maybe Finance project, offering self-hosted tracking of cashflow, net worth, and spending.
summary.usage: Sure can be self-hosted via Docker or run locally for development: run `cp .env.local.example .env.local`, `bin/setup`, and `bin/dev`, then visit http://localhost:3000; optional demo data can be loaded with `rake demo_data:default`.
summary.pros: It supports access from a browser, macOS desktop app, mobile app, API clients, and LLM agents, and offers multiple one-click deployment options including Render, PikaPods, and Hostim, all under the AGPLv3 open-source license.
summary.cons: Local development requires specific prerequisites — a Ruby version matching `.ruby-version`, PostgreSQL newer than 9.3, and Redis newer than 5.4 — and the project maintains a public dashboard tracking known performance issues on data-heavy requests.
summary.fit: Given its AGPLv3 licensing and the explicit restriction against using the "Maybe" trademark in forks, Sure likely suits individuals or communities wanting a self-hosted, community-driven personal finance tool rather than an officially branded product.

repos.name: dream-num / univer
repos.description: Build your own AI office with Univer Office SDK. Bring editing, calculation, collaboration, and file processing into your product for people and AI agents. Built on an extensible open-source core.

summary.goal: Univer is an Office SDK for embedding Office editing capabilities—spreadsheets, documents, slides, canvases, and PDFs (including Sheets and Docs)—into a developer's own application. It provides editing, calculation, collaboration, and file-processing building blocks for people and agents, using the application's own data and permissions.
summary.usage: Install with `pnpm add @univerjs/presets @univerjs/preset-sheets-core` in a Vite-based browser project, add a container element, call `createUniver` with the Sheets Core preset, then run `univerAPI.createWorkbook({})` to render an editable spreadsheet.
summary.pros: The repository's open-source Web SDK core—content models, formula and rendering engines, Facade APIs, UI foundation, and Sheets/Docs editing—is licensed under Apache-2.0 and reusable in commercial applications. Features split into content-logic and UI plugins with explicit dependency declarations, giving custom features clear boundaries and consistent extension points.
summary.cons: Older or non-standard environments may need a polyfill for `Intl.Segmenter`; developing the monorepo itself requires Node.js >=22.18, while Headless usage needs Node.js >=18.17.0, suggesting some runtime setup may be required depending on target environment. Commercial Web SDK plugins, Server SDK, and AI SDK extensions are licensed separately, and freemium evaluation includes watermarks and feature limits.
summary.fit: Univer appears suited to teams building browser-based Office editing features with bundlers like Vite, esbuild, or Webpack 5, targeting Chrome >=88, Edge >=90, Firefox >=88, Safari >=14.1, or Electron >=12, with a React 18/19 view layer (minimal support for React 16.9+/17).

repos.name: kajisho5 / ffmpeg-skill
repos.description: Local video editor for coding agents: 42 FFmpeg tools with a machine-readable contract and an MCP server, for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex. Cut, captions, reframe, loudness, platform exports. No cloud, no API keys.

summary.goal: ffmpeg-skill is an Agent Skill that gives coding agents such as Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or any MCP client the ability to edit video footage using a local FFmpeg installation and then verify the output. It runs without cloud services or API keys, relying only on the Python standard library.
summary.usage: Install and configure it with `npx ffmpeg-skill setup`, which installs the skill for detected agents, installs FFmpeg if it is missing, and ends with a `doctor` check. Tools can also be run directly via `npx ffmpeg-skill` or invoked as MCP tools from an MCP client.
summary.pros: All processing happens locally, so footage is never uploaded. It follows a documented probe-edit-verify workflow across 42 tools, 12 of which are marked stable, and exposes a machine-readable contract so an agent can automatically discover each tool's capabilities and arguments.
summary.cons: Setup requires Node 16+ and Python 3.10+ to already be present, since the installer does not install either. Optional local transcription for captions needs a separately installed speech engine; without one, `--transcribe` refuses to run. The overall `ok` status from `doctor` can read false even when most individual tools remain usable, since any single missing FFmpeg capability is enough to trip it.
summary.fit: This appears suited to users who want an AI coding agent to perform local, verifiable video editing (cutting, captioning, exporting) without sending media to external services, particularly within the Claude Code / Cursor / Codex / MCP ecosystem the README describes.

repos.name: Nutlope / hallmark
repos.description: Anti-AI-slop design skill for Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex.

summary.goal: Hallmark is a design skill for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and OpenCode, made by Together AI and documented at https://www.usehallmark.com. It aims to generate web pages that avoid common visual tells associated with AI-generated design, applying a baseline of checks before building a page.
summary.usage: Install with `npx skills add nutlope/hallmark -g`. Invoked harnesses can run commands such as `/hallmark redesign <path>` or `/hallmark audit <path>`, or a described build request, depending on the tool.
summary.pros: The project offers fifty selectable themes plus a custom design mode, dedicated redesign and audit commands, 755 openly licensed credited photographs, and an automated lint pass (sloplint) checking pages against known AI-style design tells.
summary.cons: The tool requires Node 18 or later, and its browser-based checks (such as rendering and screenshots) need an additional global install of puppeteer-core plus Chrome; without these, only static checks run.
summary.fit: Hallmark appears best suited to teams already using Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, or OpenCode, since it integrates as a skill or plugin within those harnesses rather than as a standalone application.

repos.name: cloudflare / security-audit-skill
repos.description: A coding-agent skill for multi-phase security audits with independently verified, machine-readable findings

summary.goal: security-audit is a skill that turns a coding agent into a security auditor, running audits through six phases: reconnaissance, coverage-led hunting, candidate validation, structured output, independent record verification, and target-neutral reporting. It is the single-repo starting point from which Cloudflare's multi-stage vulnerability discovery harness evolved.
summary.usage: Install via the Skills CLI with `npx skills add https://github.com/cloudflare/security-audit-skill --skill security-audit` (add `--global` for a user-level install). Inside the codebase to audit, ask the coding agent to run a request such as `security audit this codebase`; an unspecified output directory defaults to `~/security-audit-skill/<repo-name>/run-<N>`.
summary.pros: The workflow uses adversarial validation, where the agent that verifies a finding is never the one that found it, and produces three distinct verdicts (confirmed, needs_validation, rejected) validated against a schema. Cloudflare's test runs reportedly found a single run caught roughly half the vulnerabilities that repeated runs found in total, since ledgers and findings are additive across runs.
summary.cons: Executing target code (builds, tests, fuzzers) requires an OS-enforced sandbox that disables external networking, uses a sanitized allowlisted environment, enforces resource limits, and restricts writes to scratch paths; without it, leads reportedly stay marked needs_validation rather than being executed. This suggests full use of the skill may be difficult without existing sandbox infrastructure.
summary.fit: Given the sandboxing, Node.js, and parallel-sub-agent model requirements, the skill seems best suited to teams already using capable coding agents and willing to invest in isolated execution environments, rather than serving as a lightweight, drop-in audit tool.

repos.name: milind-soni / OpenMausBot
repos.description: Open-source Grok Bot alternative with a virtual machine that bots can use

summary.goal: OpenMausBot is described as an open-source, independent project inspired by Grok Bot, providing a desktop chat application where multiple AI agents—each running locally via the Claude or Codex CLI—act as individual bots with their own model, computer, and connected apps.
summary.usage: Users can download a signed macOS/Windows/Linux package from https://github.com/milind-soni/OpenMausBot, install from source with `pnpm install`, or install it globally with `npm install -g openmausbot` and then run the `openmausbot` command to start a local server and open the chat interface.
summary.pros: Documented features suggest several potential advantages, including bring-your-own-agent CLIs that reuse a user's existing logins (no new accounts), local-first data storage in `~/.openmausbot`, permission-based approval cards before risky actions, and app connectivity through Composio.
summary.cons: The Windows installer is not yet code-signed, which triggers a SmartScreen 'unknown publisher' warning; Ubuntu support remains in beta with Wayland-based host control disabled pending issue #345; and in the CLI/server mode, API keys are stored as plaintext in config.json rather than encrypted.
summary.fit: The project appears best suited to users who already hold Claude, Codex, or Grok CLI subscriptions and prefer a local, multi-agent chat interface over a cloud-hosted single-agent product, running on macOS, Windows, or Ubuntu 24.04 with Node 24+.

repos.name: pingdotgg / t3code
repos.description: The best way to control Claude Code, Codex and more from any computer or phone

summary.goal: T3 Code is an open-source MIT-licensed control plane for coding agents, running agents like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode, Grok Build, Antigravity, Kiro, Pi, Muse Code, fx, and ACP agents on the user's own machine via one interface, letting a thread be started on desktop and approved from a phone.
summary.usage: Install the desktop app from https://t3.codes/download or a package manager, or install the CLI with `curl -fsSL https://t3.codes/install.sh | sh` (PowerShell: `irm https://t3.codes/install.ps1 | iex`) and run `t3` to start the server and open the web app; `npx t3@latest` allows a one-time trial. It requires at least one agent already installed and signed in, e.g. via `claude auth login` or `codex login`.
summary.pros: It does not resell tokens, instead using the user's existing agent subscriptions; it unifies desktop, web, and phone clients around one server and the same threads; it includes built-in git support with per-thread worktrees and one-button commit, push, and pull-request actions; remote access is supported via local network, Tailscale, or T3 Connect.
summary.cons: Because it depends on externally installed and signed-in agents rather than bundling them, at least one separate agent (e.g. Claude Code or Codex CLI) must be set up and authenticated before T3 Code can be used, which is an added prerequisite step beyond installing T3 Code itself.
summary.fit: It appears suited for developers who already use one or more coding agents and want a single, performant interface to manage and switch between them across desktop, web, and mobile, including remote approval workflows; it may be less relevant for users without any coding agent already installed.

repos.name: anthropics / skills
repos.description: Public repository for Agent Skills

summary.goal: This repository provides Anthropic's reference implementation of Skills for Claude — folders containing instructions, scripts, and resources that Claude loads dynamically to perform specialized tasks such as document creation, data analysis, or workflow automation.
summary.usage: Skills can be installed in Claude Code as a plugin marketplace via `/plugin marketplace add anthropics/skills`, followed by `/plugin install document-skills@anthropic-agent-skills` or `/plugin install example-skills@anthropic-agent-skills`. They are also available directly to paid Claude.ai plans and through the Claude API.
summary.pros: Many skills, including the docx, pdf, pptx, and xlsx document-handling skills that power Claude's document capabilities in production, are released under the Apache 2.0 open-source license, giving developers reusable examples of complex, actively used skills.
summary.cons: The README states these skills are provided for demonstration and educational purposes only, and that actual Claude behavior may differ from what is shown, so users are advised to test skills thoroughly in their own environment before relying on them for critical tasks.
summary.fit: This project appears best suited for developers seeking patterns and inspiration for building their own Claude skills rather than for teams needing a guaranteed production-ready toolset out of the box.

repos.name: thedotmack / claude-mem
repos.description: Persistent Context Across Sessions for Every Agent –  Captures everything your agent does during sessions, compresses it with AI, and injects relevant context back into future sessions. Works with Claude Code, OpenClaw, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, Copilot, OpenCode + More

summary.goal: Claude-Mem gives coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and OpenCode persistent memory across sessions. While the agent works, a second observer agent records tool activity, so the next session can start with a condensed index of prior context instead of from zero.
summary.usage: Install with `npx claude-mem install`, or inside Claude Code run `/plugin marketplace add thedotmack/claude-mem` followed by `/plugin install claude-mem`, then restart Claude Code; starting with the second session in a project, prior memory loads automatically.
summary.pros: Search uses a token-efficient three-step MCP workflow (search, timeline, get_observations), so agents fetch full observation details only for IDs they actually need. Content wrapped in `<private>` tags is never stored, and the project is released under the Apache License 2.0.
summary.cons: Copilot CLI, Goose, Roo Code, Warp, and Zed can only search existing memory since their sessions are not recorded, so coverage depends on which agent is used. Installing the npm package globally only sets up the SDK/library, not the plugin hooks, so the documented npx installer is likely still needed for a full setup.
summary.fit: Likely fits developers already using a supported coding agent who want continuity between sessions without manual note-taking. Memory is stored locally under `~/.claude-mem` by default, with cloud sync and team sharing offered as opt-in extensions.

repos.name: Jakeschincariol / instagram-agent-skill
repos.description: Thirteen Claude skills that run an Instagram account: Reels off 26 scored hook formulas, a viral research skill, a caption linter, and a humanizer. Free, MIT.

summary.goal: instagram-agent-skill provides thirteen Claude skills intended to support running an Instagram account, covering Reel scripting, caption writing, profile scoring, weekly planning, and a humanizer that strips slop vocabulary and invisible characters from drafts. The README states it is free, MIT-licensed, and requires no signup or API key.
summary.usage: Installation is done by pasting the repository URL https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/instagram-agent-skill into Claude, or by running git clone https://github.com/Jakeschincariol/instagram-agent-skill.git followed by copying the skills folders, or via /plugin install. Users are told to first fill in templates/voice.md, then invoke commands such as /ig-reel or local scripts like python3 hookscore.py hooks.txt.
summary.pros: The five Python tools (hookscore.py, beats.py, caption.py, humanize.py, detect.py, swipe.py) reportedly run locally with no dependencies or network calls. An approval gate means nothing is posted automatically, and the caption tool enforces Instagram's current five-hashtag cap effective 18 December 2025. The README also reports an AUC of 0.83 for flagging deliberately weak hooks.
summary.cons: The README states these skills do not post to Instagram directly; real publishing requires a Meta developer app, linked Page, long-lived token, and app review, which the skill cannot provide. It also discloses that the hook scorer's ability to pick winning hooks among good ones is weak, at AUC 0.56, close to a coin flip.
summary.fit: This appears suited to Instagram creators using Claude Code who want drafting, scoring, and planning assistance while retaining manual control over posting. Without Claude Code, the README notes the five Python tools are unavailable, so project-local or plugin installation seems best for full functionality.

repos.name: HKUDS / DeepTutor
repos.description: DeepTutor: Lifelong Personalized Tutoring. https://deeptutor.info/.

summary.goal: DeepTutor (HKUDS/DeepTutor) is documented as an agent-native learning workspace that connects tutoring, research, content creation, and practice in a single extensible system, released under the Apache 2.0 license.
summary.usage: The README documents installing with `pip install -U "deeptutor[full]"` followed by `deeptutor init` and `deeptutor start` to launch backend and frontend together, or running `docker run --rm --name deeptutor -p 127.0.0.1:3782:3782 -v deeptutor-data:/app/data ghcr.io/hkuds/deeptutor:latest` to trial the full web app without installing Python or Node.js.
summary.pros: Documented capabilities include a shared runtime across multiple learning modes (Chat, Quiz, Research, Visualize, Solve, Mastery Path, Reading), a connected workspace linking Chat, Books, Reading, Practice, Task Board, and Calendar, grounded knowledge retrieval through multiple RAG engines (LlamaIndex, PageIndex, GraphRAG, LightRAG), consultable agent partners/subagents, and an inspectable three-layer memory system.
summary.cons: Full installation requires Python 3.11–3.14 and Node.js 20.9+ as stated prerequisites, so environments outside that range likely need adjustment before setup succeeds.
summary.fit: Based on its CLI/SDK design for headless operation and NDJSON output described for agent-driven runs, DeepTutor appears best suited for users wanting a self-hosted, extensible tutoring platform that can also be automated or embedded by other agents, rather than a lightweight single-purpose chatbot.

repos.name: pbakaus / impeccable
repos.description: The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder, review with critique and audit, catch AI slop before it ships.

summary.goal: Impeccable is presented as a design vocabulary for a coding agent, offering commands like polish, bolder, critique, and audit to steer and review AI-generated interface work. It includes a slop detector built from 62 deterministic rules and a total of 24 commands covering steering, review, finishing, and setup tasks.
summary.usage: From a project root, it is installed with `npx impeccable install`, after which the coding tool is reloaded and `/impeccable init` is run to generate a PRODUCT.md context file. The detector can also run standalone, for example `npx impeccable detect src/` to scan a directory from the CLI or CI.
summary.pros: The detector relies on 62 deterministic rules rather than an LLM or API key, and can run automatically as an agent hook that scans edited files before an agent reports work as done. It also supports GitHub Actions annotations and SARIF 2.1.0 output for code-scanning integration.
summary.cons: Live mode only edits a local checkout, and the README cautions against injecting it into a deployed site or weakening a production CSP to use it. It also notes that applying copy edits runs an optional package.json validation script with the user's own permissions, so reviewing that script before using live mode in an unfamiliar repo is advised.
summary.fit: The README lists compatibility with many coding agents and tools, including Claude Code, Cursor, Codex CLI, GitHub Copilot, Devin, Replit Agent, Gemini CLI, Grok Build, OpenCode, Google Antigravity, Kiro, Trae, Rovo Dev, Qoder, Mistral Vibe, Pi, Hermes Agent, DeepSeek Harness, and Veto, with full docs at https://impeccable.style/docs. This breadth suggests Impeccable likely fits best into projects already using one of these supported agents rather than standalone or unsupported toolchains.

repos.name: sherlock-project / sherlock
repos.description: Hunt down social media accounts by username across social networks

summary.goal: Sherlock is a command-line tool documented as helping users search for social media accounts tied to a specific username across 400+ social networks.
summary.usage: Installation can be done with `pipx install sherlock-project` (pip or uv are listed as alternatives), via Docker with `docker run -it --rm sherlock/sherlock`, or `dnf install sherlock-project`. To search, run `sherlock user123` for one username or `sherlock user1 user2 user3` for several; found accounts are saved to text files, and `sherlock --help` lists all available flags.
summary.pros: The README lists multiple installation routes (pipx/pip/uv, Docker, dnf), export options in CSV and XLSX formats, proxy support via `--proxy`, and flags for filtering specific sites, adjusting timeouts, and controlling output verbosity.
summary.cons: The documentation notes that third-party packages for ParrotOS and Ubuntu 24.04 are currently reported as broken, and that community-maintained packages for Debian, Ubuntu, Homebrew, Kali, and BlackArch are not directly supported or maintained by the Sherlock Project itself.
summary.fit: Based on the documented features, this tool may be best suited for OSINT-style username enumeration on systems with Python/pipx or Docker available; it is currently at version 0.16.0 and distributed under the MIT license.

repos.name: AgriciDaniel / claude-seo
repos.description: Universal SEO skill for Claude Code. 26 sub-skills + 19 sub-agents covering technical SEO, E-E-A-T, schema, GEO/AEO, agent readiness (Lighthouse Agentic Browsing, WebMCP, llms.txt), backlinks, local SEO, e-commerce, international SEO, Google APIs, and PDF/Excel reporting. 9 optional extensions for live SEO data.

summary.goal: Claude SEO is described as a free, open-source SEO audit plugin for Claude Code that, given a website, runs a full SEO audit in 10 to 15 minutes covering technical SEO, Core Web Vitals, E-E-A-T content quality, Schema.org structured data, AI search (GEO), and local and e-commerce SEO, then produces a prioritized action plan.
summary.usage: Inside Claude Code, it is installed by running `/plugin marketplace add AgriciDaniel/claude-seo`, `/plugin install claude-seo@agricidaniel-claude-seo`, and `/seo setup` in order; audits are then run with commands such as `/seo audit <url>`.
summary.pros: The README states the tool is built from 29 sub-skills and 20 specialist agents, with up to 17 agents able to work on a site in parallel, is free with no per-site pricing or usage limits, and saves reports locally as Markdown, PDF, and JSON files.
summary.cons: According to the README, a full `/seo audit` uses more of a user's Claude plan because five agents run on Opus; without optional Google API keys, Core Web Vitals are lab estimates and indexing is inferred from the page, and pages requiring scrolling or clicking can produce noisy results.
summary.fit: The README positions the tool for SEO agencies seeking recurring audits, in-house SEO teams at SaaS, publishing, or e-commerce companies, and freelance SEO consultants who want to show audit results before writing a proposal.

repos.name: heygen-com / hyperframes
repos.description: Open-source AI video editor: edit your own footage, or create and remake any video with Claude Code, Codex or the free Studio app. Write HTML, render MP4. By HeyGen.

summary.goal: HyperFrames is described as HeyGen's open-source (Apache 2.0) AI video editor and framework for turning HTML, CSS, JavaScript, media, and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos, intended for both people and coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor.
summary.usage: Developers can install skills for a coding agent with `npx skills add heygen-com/hyperframes`, then scaffold a project with `npx hyperframes init my-video`, preview it with `npx hyperframes preview`, and render it with `npx hyperframes render`. The README states this requires Node.js 22+ and FFmpeg, and that rendering can also run in the cloud or on AWS Lambda.
summary.pros: The README lists HTML-native authoring with no React requirement, an agent-friendly non-interactive CLI, deterministic rendering (same input produces the same output), no mandatory build step, support for multiple animation libraries (GSAP, CSS, Lottie, Three.js, Anime.js, WAAPI), and an Apache 2.0 license with no per-render fees.
summary.cons: Running the CLI requires the documented prerequisites of Node.js 22+ and FFmpeg. The Studio app's Pro tier costs $25 a month for extra models and 25,000 credits monthly, and the README notes that community-maintained skills are not maintained by the core project and should be reviewed before use, which suggests their quality or support level may be inconsistent.
summary.fit: Based on the documented use cases, HyperFrames appears suited to developers and teams generating video programmatically through AI coding agents, CI pipelines, or automated content workflows, as well as non-technical users via the Studio app, though the README does not detail its fit for every production scenario.

repos.name: vercel-labs / agent-browser
repos.description: Browser automation CLI for AI agents

summary.goal: agent-browser is a native Rust command-line tool that gives AI agents browser automation: it opens pages, reads them as an accessibility-style tree, and lets the agent act on elements from the shell. The core loop uses `snapshot`, which returns the page as compact text with a ref (e.g. `@e1`) per element; the agent acts on a ref, then re-snapshots to check the result.
summary.usage: Install with `npm install -g agent-browser`, then run `agent-browser install` once to download Chrome for Testing. A documented quick start is: `agent-browser open example.com`, `agent-browser snapshot -i`, `agent-browser click @e1`, `agent-browser get url`, and `agent-browser close`.
summary.pros: Beyond refs, the CLI also supports CSS selectors, text, XPath, and semantic locators (e.g. `find role button`). It can drive multiple browser engines (Chrome for Testing by default, Lightpanda, Obscura) and cloud providers (Browserbase, Browserless, Browser Use, Kernel, AgentCore), and ships native binaries for macOS, Linux, and Windows.
summary.cons: A click is reported as failed rather than succeeding when the target element is hidden, disabled, outside the viewport, or covered by another element (e.g. a consent banner), requiring the agent to dismiss the obstruction and take a new snapshot before retrying. Building from source also requires Node.js 24 or later, pnpm 11 or later, and Rust.
summary.fit: Given its stdio MCP server (`agent-browser mcp`) and documented integration guidance for Next.js/Vercel and eve agents, it appears aimed at AI-agent-driven browser automation pipelines, though teams without a Node/Rust toolchain may find source builds less convenient.
